inbox.subject: Boston pod offline since 11:40pm
inbox.body:
Alex, Jordan, Sanjay,

Our office network in Boston went down at 11:40pm. Nobody on the pod can reach the console or the household inbox. I'm on my phone hotspot but it keeps dropping. Agents are still closing routine tasks but anything that needs a care lead handoff is stacking up. I've asked Devon and Kim to log in from home.

Will update within the hour.
Marisol Reyes
Boston care lead

inbox.subject: RE: Boston pod offline since 11:40pm
inbox.body:
Update: ISP says a fiber cut on their side, no ETA. Devon is online from home, Kim's home connection is too slow for the console. Handoff queue is at 140 and climbing. Two families called the after hours line asking why nobody answered about pharmacy refills. I called both back.

Marisol

inbox.subject: RE: Boston pod offline since 11:40pm
inbox.body:
Network back at 5:15am. Total down about five and a half hours. Backlog peaked at 212 handoffs across 310 Boston households. We're working it oldest first and I think we clear it by 11am. Three items were time sensitive (two refills, one home aide no show) and all three are handled.

We need a backup line for this office. This is the second time since summer.

Marisol

inbox.subject: Boston outage overnight: preliminary notes
inbox.body:
Alex,

Quick summary on the Boston outage overnight. Platform was fine, this was the Boston office ISP only. Agents kept running and closed about 70% of tasks as normal. The gap was care lead handoffs, which assume console access. I'll have a written timeline before the 3:30pm review. Proposal: LTE failover router for every pod office, roughly $400 per site plus data.

Sanjay

inbox.subject: Boston hotspot use
inbox.body:
Alex,

Marisol and Devon used personal hotspots and a home connection to reach household data overnight. Both are on managed laptops with VPN so I'm not worried about exposure, but I want it in the incident log and I want a written rule for next time. No customer notice needed from a privacy standpoint.

Nadia

inbox.subject: November forecast: $1M ARR gap
inbox.body:
Alex,

Forecast attached ahead of tomorrow. We closed October at ARR $18M. The plan for year end is $19M. With what's in pipeline for November and December, I have us landing at about $18.0M to $18.2M, so call it a $1M gap.

Most of the shortfall is at Work deals that slipped into Q1, plus Family adds running about 60 households a month under plan. Harborline doesn't help 2026 ARR unless we sign before December 15.

Three options in the deck. Let's go through them at 11:30am.

Julian

inbox.subject: Harborline: partnership deal points remain outstanding
inbox.body:
Alex,

The partnership deal points remain outstanding after Friday's redline from Harborline Mutual. Where we are:

1. January launch. They want all 40,000 employees live January 1. That's about 1,600 households entering setup in January. Jordan says we can set up 800 and keep the promise.
2. Repricing. They pushed back on repricing at renewal if activation passes 6%. Our $6 price assumes 4%.
3. Reporting. They asked for site level reports. Our floor is 25 people per cell and I said we won't move it.

Price at $6 per employee per month is agreed, worth $2.9M new ARR. I'd like our positions settled at 2pm so I can send a reply Thursday.

Tomás

inbox.subject: Harborline capacity plan due Wednesday
inbox.body:
Alex,

Heads up that the capacity plan for Harborline is due to you Wednesday. Draft covers a phased January: 800 households set up from January 1, the rest in February, plus what it takes to go faster. Right now 48 care leads, ceiling of 120 Family households each. Going to 1,600 in January means 9 more care leads hired and trained by mid December, which I don't think the pipeline supports.

Boston will eat some of my morning so I may slip to Wednesday evening. Will flag at the 10am.

Jordan

inbox.subject: October recruiting numbers
inbox.body:
Hi Alex,

October numbers ahead of our 1pm. Active pipeline is down 15% from September, worse than the 8% drop we saw the month before. The People & Culture searches are hit hardest: Head of People has two finalists left after one withdrew, and the Senior People Partner search has no one past first round. Care lead applications are holding up better.

Lena Okafor's references are in and both are strong. I'll bring options to rebuild the People & Culture slate.

Best,
Grace

inbox.subject: Dad update
inbox.body:
Hey,

Talked to my sister. Dad's surgery is confirmed for Wednesday at 8. He's in a lot of pain but clear headed. I'm on the 7:15am. Thanks for driving me, I know your morning is packed and you finally have the mammogram.

Love you,
Sam

Riverside Women's Imaging

inbox.subject: Harborline timing
inbox.body:
Alex,

Heard from Julian that Harborline may slip into January. Not a problem for the board, but I'd like a 15 minute call before Thanksgiving on where the deal points land and what it does to the 2026 number. Any slot next week works.

Helen

inbox.subject: Thanksgiving

Alex, are you and Sam still coming the 26th? Aunt Donna says yes but I want to hear it from you. Bring nothing, or bring pie.

inbox.subject: Eval results: refill agent v4

Alex,

Refill agent v4 passed the weekly eval set at 96% versus 93% for v3, no new safety flags. Dr. Patel signed off on the escalation rules yesterday. Planning to roll to 20% of households Thursday unless you object.

Wen

inbox.subject: Agenda for 1:1

Two things for today: Standing Plan template v3 and why partner portal confirmations are stuck at 40%. Happy to push if Boston takes over the afternoon.

Priya

newsletters.title: Employers rethink eldercare benefits for 2027
newsletters.body: Benefits leaders surveyed this fall say eldercare support is moving from pilot to standard offering, with per employee pricing replacing per use fees. Insurers are the most active buyers, but most want activation guarantees in contract.

newsletters.title: Hiring cooled again in October
newsletters.body: Startup hiring pipelines shrank for a third straight month. People operations roles saw the steepest falloff in qualified applicants, while frontline service roles held steady.

newsletters.title: New York home aide shortages ahead of winter
newsletters.body: Agencies across the five boroughs report longer fill times for home aide shifts, with weekend coverage the hardest to staff.
